question: Which of the following is the primary constituent of naturally occurring mineral magnetite on Earth?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Iron Oxide**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Iron Oxide** is the **primary component **of **naturally occurring mineral magnetite on Earth**.
 
• **Magnetite** is a **rock mineral **and one of the most important **iron ore minerals with chemical formula is iron (II, III) oxide, Fe2+Fe3+2O4**.
 
• It is found in **igneous, metamorphic, and sedimentary rocks**.
 
• It is a major **component of steel manufacturing and is also used as a catalyst **in the **Haber process **for making ammonia as a pigment for paints and ceramics etc.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Its **IUPAC (chemical) **name is **Ferrous Oxide**.
 
• Magnesium oxide is a white hygroscopic solid mineral that occurs naturally as periclase and is a source of magnesium.
 
• Aluminum oxide (Al2O3), is an inert, odorless, white amorphous material often used in industrial ceramics.
 
• **Calcium oxide (CaO), **commonly known as **quicklime or burnt lime**, is a widely used chemical compound use in the** manufacturing of cement, paper, and high-grade steel**.
